---
# GENERATED by scripts/sync-claude.ts — edit scripts/sync-claude.ts instead
description: Review the current branch's diff like a strict senior engineer and print the verdict as plain text
argument-hint: "[base-branch]"
allowed-tools: Task, Agent, Read, Grep, Glob, Bash(git diff:*), Bash(git log:*), Bash(git status:*), Bash(git rev-parse:*), Bash(git merge-base:*), Bash(git branch:*)
---

Review the current branch against `${1:-main}` and print the verdict as plain text.

This command must work headless (`claude -p "/review"`): never ask a question, never wait for
input, never edit, commit or push anything. It needs no browser tools — only /design-loop and
/test-feature require the Playwright MCP server.

1. Resolve the base ref `${1:-main}` with `git rev-parse --verify "${1:-main}^{commit}"`. If it
   does not exist locally, try `origin/${1:-main}` once and say which ref you used. If neither
   resolves, print `unknown base ref "${1:-main}"` and stop.
2. `git diff --name-only ${1:-main}...HEAD` for the changed files, then
   `git diff ${1:-main}...HEAD` for the diff. Three dots, always — the merge-base diff, not the
   two-dot one. If the diff is empty, print exactly `nothing to review`, nothing else, and stop:
   no explanation of why it is empty, no offer to review the working tree instead.
3. Cap what you hand over at ~60 KB: include whole per-file diffs while they fit, then a head
   slice of the first file that does not, and name the files that were cut short or left out so
   the reviewer knows to read them itself.
4. Delegate the judgement to the **code-reviewer** subagent (one Task call). Give it: the repo
   root, the base ref, the changed-file list, which files are truncated or omitted, and the diff.
   The subagent is read-only (Read/Grep/Glob) — it reads surrounding context itself. Do not
   review the diff yourself and do not soften what it reports.
5. Print the reviewer's answer verbatim, in this exact shape, nothing before the VERDICT line —
   no preamble, no summary, no markdown headings, no code fences:

```
VERDICT: <APPROVE | APPROVE WITH NITS | REQUEST CHANGES>

[SEVERITY] path/to/file.ts:LINE — one-line title
Risk: why this matters in practice.
Fix: concrete change.
```

   Severity is one of BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, NIT; findings are sorted BLOCKER first; the
   separator between `file:line` and the title is an em dash ("—"), not a hyphen; every finding
   is exactly three lines. `REQUEST CHANGES` requires at least one finding in that format.
   With no findings, print only the VERDICT line.
6. If the answer does not match that format, ask the subagent exactly once more, appending
   `Your previous output violated the format. Output only the required format.` If the retry is
   still malformed, print one line saying so followed by the raw text — never invent a verdict.
7. A BLOCKER is reported in the text (the agent-workflows CLI, `aw review`, maps it to exit
   code 2; a slash command cannot set an exit code). Never fix the code here and never ask questions —
   this command reviews, the human decides.

The last line you print is either `nothing to review` or the last `Fix:` line. Never close with
a question, an offer, a next step or a summary: under `claude -p` there is nobody to answer.
